checks: Scaling the normal by its positive norm and making the shift nonnegative preserves the pair up to swapping. For unit normals and centers in the common radius-R₀ ball, every s≥2R₀ gives the average 1/2; the possibly nonempty upper cap at s=2R₀ is null. Its value is represented at the compact parameter endpoint. Both parameter-dependent indicators converge off null limiting hyperplanes, so the compact minimum is continuous and the maximum over K is attained.

The paired centroid lower bound applies for all shifts after exchanging the two signs. At zero shift the average is the ordinary cap probability, so p_K(y) is bounded above by the ordinary depth at the same y. A simplex has ordinary maximum Γ_d and consequently paired maximum Γ_d.

Assuming the paired maximum equals Γ_d forces p_K(g)=Γ_d. The strict parent excludes every nonzero shift from the compact active set. The remaining unit normals are exactly the centroid through-cap equalities, a compact nonempty set.

For a nonsimplex the attained ordinary maximum is greater than Γ_d. For every active normal the cap at y_* must strictly gain over its cap at g. Increasing the threshold cannot gain mass, so u·(y_*−g)<0 for every active normal. Compactness gives a common a>0, and the stated relative neighborhood contains the entire active set. Its compact complement has a uniformly positive initial gap that persists for small t by joint continuity.

The center g+tv is in K by convexity. In the relative neighborhood both thresholds u·g±s change by t(u·v)<−ta/2. If t‖v‖<ρ/4 and s<ρ/4, the swept slabs lie between signed levels −ρ/2 and ρ/2 relative to g. The inner-ball sections there have radius at least √3ρ/2 and therefore a uniform positive (d−1)-volume. Each cap strictly gains, including when s=0 and both caps are the same. Compactness and continuity then make the new minimum strictly greater than Γ_d.

The ambient supremum equals the attained maximum on K because strict separation gives exterior centers a zero-mass shift-zero cap. With the stated TV convention, two cap probabilities each change by at most TV, hence their average, the infimum over a common set of pairs, and the supremum over a common set of centers obey the same bound.

Uniform support-function convergence ensures each interior point of the full-dimensional limit eventually belongs to the approximants. Every exterior point eventually stays outside. The null boundary and the common outer ball give L¹ convergence, and the inner ball bounds the normalized-volume denominators away from zero. Thus D_pair is continuous on the fixed-ball class.

The fixed-ball class is compact by Blaschke selection and closedness of the inclusions. Distance to the nonempty set of full-dimensional simplices is 1-Lipschitz even without assuming that set is closed. The ε-distance subclass is compact and excludes simplices. The stated nonempty case has a positive attained minimum by rigidity and continuity.

Strict centroid tails leave only shift-zero minimizers, and movement toward an ordinary maximizer strictly improves every such pair and its neighborhood for a nonsimplex.
